# dsh-plugin-default-workspace

A small DSH plugin that pins the **no-context fallback Workspace of new
Sessions** to one folder, ch

osen in the Settings dialog, and keeps the
provisional **New Session** row out of the Workspace list

until its composer
holds input.
## Why this exists

DSH chooses the Workspace of a new Session from context, never from
configuration:
| Situation | Stock DSH behavior | With this plugin |
| A Session holding a conversation is open in some folder | the new Session stays in that folder | u

nchanged |
| The app opens on a saved Session holding a conversation | that Session is restored | un

changed |
| An explicit target is passed (a workspace row's **+**, *add workspace*) | that target is

used | unchanged |
| **Nothing to go on**: no saved selection, a saved Session that no longer exist
s, or a saved/current **empty New Session** (nothing ever sent) | the *most recently active* Workspa

ce | **the folder chosen in Settings** |
| **The Session you are viewing is archived** | the main se
lection is cleared and the app drops to its *choose a Workspace* hero | **a new Session in that Sess
ion's own Workspace**, or the chosen folder when it had no Workspace |

An empty New Session is not "already conversing in another folder": DSH marks a
Session `blank` (`Se

ssionSummary.blank`) until its first turn starts, and that
flag is what decides the last-but-one row

above. Clicking a workspace row and
typing still starts the conversation in that folder; the folder

only takes over
once there is a conversation in it.

Archiving is the one case where the folder that comes back is *not* the chosen
one: the conversation

is gone but the project is not, so archiving a Session in
`D:\CodeProjects\Moltenfrost` leaves you

in `Moltenfrost` with a fresh New
Session. A Session that belonged to no Workspace has no folder of

its own to
keep, so it falls back to the chosen folder — the same rule as the row above.
Only cleari

ng a main Session is honoured this way; archiving any other row
navigates nothing, exactly as before

g a main Session is honoured this way; archiving any other row
navigates nothing, exactly as before.

The Host owns no setting for this. The only "default workspace" concept in DSH
(`workspaceRegistry.i

nitializeDefault`, `<Documents>\deepseek-harness\default-workspace`)
is created once on a pristine i

nstall and requires an empty Workspace registry
*and* empty Session history, so it cannot be repoint

ed on an installation that
already has Sessions.
## The New Session row

Stock DSH draws the selected blank Session in the Workspace list right away: the
row is labeled **Ne

w Session** and exists before anything was typed into it. On
an app that opens on an empty New Sessi

on, that is a row in the sidebar the
moment the window appears.

This plugin keeps that one row out of the list until the composer holds
something:

racter typed, pasted, or inserted -> the row appears, without a
reload and without sending anything;
- the composer cleared again -> the row hides again.

While a turn is being submitted the draft clears *before* the Session stops
being blank, so the row

keeps its state for that moment instead of blinking out
between the two events; the Session's first
turn then releases the rule for good.

Only the *current* blank Session is affected; every other blank Session is
already hidden by DSH, an

d a Session becomes an ordinary row at its first turn,
at which point this policy releases it. The S

ession itself, its unsent draft, and
every navigation rule are untouched: the policy hides the row,

it never changes
which Session the list contains. Choosing **Follow DSH** on the settings page
relea
ses the row as well.

The hide rule is a stylesheet keyed by Session id, not a change applied to the
row. That ordering is

the point: a row hidden *after* the list has laid it out
would make the rows below jump down and th

en back up — clicking **New Session**
would visibly bounce the list. Two things make the ordering ho

back up — clicking **New Session**
would visibly bounce the list. Two things make the ordering hold:

- the navigation flow pre-hides the Session at `connectBlank`, the moment the id
is known and before

`replaceMain` makes its row visible — this is what covers
the *first* click, when the id is new and

no rule exists for it yet;
- the row policy subscribes to the Session projection as early as it can

, so a
blank that enters the list by another route is still ahead of the render.

A blank that is already the main selection is not pre-hidden (reopening the blank
you are looking at

keeps its row exactly as it was), and the stylesheet is

## Choosing the folder

Settings carries one page from this plugin, **Default folder**, as its own
navigation tab (`settings
.section`, order 30 — after the shipped sections):

- the selector lists every registered Workspace by path, plus **Follow DSH**,
which switches the plu

pens the same folder chooser the Workspace UI
uses — the Desktop preload dialog when the shell expos

es it, otherwise the
Host chooser through `uiWorkspace.pickDirectory()`. A folder the Workspace
regi

stry does not know yet is registered first, exactly like
**Add workspace…** (`uiWorkspace.workspaces

localStorage under
`dsh.default-workspace.settings` and is read at every routing decision, so it
app
lies to the next New Session with no reload and no re-apply.
[该节后续省略]
### Why localStorage

The Host settings document edits fields a plugin declares with `.volatile()` in
its exported `Config

` schema, which comes from `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`. A
plugin mounted as a `file:///…` Loader row

resolves its own imports relative to
its directory, so that bare specifier is unreachable without sh

ipping a
`node_modules` next to the plugin. The preference is therefore browser-local,
which is also

where the policy lives. The cost is that it is per browser origin
and invisible to the Host configu

ration file; the benefit is a plugin with no
dependencies at all.
